# FEATURE: Parser Keys

| Field       | Value |
|-------------|-------|
| Version     | 20261014 V1 |
| Description | Bare, quoted, and dotted key forms, and the key-definition rules that reject redefinition. |
| Depends On  | ARCHITECTURE.md, FEATURE-Parser-Strings.md, FEATURE-Parser-Lexical-Scalars.md |
| Provides    | bare, quoted, and dotted key parsing with redefinition checks |
| Consumes    | None |

## Questions

- None.

## Purpose

Parse bare keys (`A-Za-z0-9_-`), quoted keys (basic or literal strings), and dotted keys that create intermediate tables. Reject defining the same key twice. A bare key and a quoted key with the same name are equivalent. A key that holds an integer cannot later be used as a table.

## Programmatic Acceptance

=== AC keys-bare-round-trip ===
Intent: A bare key decodes as the named key with a tagged value.
Requires: executable=go; scope=test

import json
import subprocess
import sys

build = subprocess.run(
    ["go", "build", "-o", "toml-decoder", "./cmd/toml-decoder"],
    capture_output=True, text=True,
)
print(build.stderr, file=sys.stderr)
assert build.returncode == 0

key = "bare-key_1"
value = "5"
source = f"{key} = {value}\n"
result = subprocess.run(["./toml-decoder"], input=source, capture_output=True, text=True)
print(result.stderr, file=sys.stderr)
assert result.returncode == 0
decoded = json.loads(result.stdout)
assert decoded == {key: {"type": "integer", "value": value}}
=== END AC keys-bare-round-trip ===

=== AC keys-dotted-round-trip ===
Intent: A dotted key creates the intermediate table and stores the value at its leaf.
Requires: executable=go; scope=test

import json
import subprocess
import sys

build = subprocess.run(
    ["go", "build", "-o", "toml-decoder", "./cmd/toml-decoder"],
    capture_output=True, text=True,
)
print(build.stderr, file=sys.stderr)
assert build.returncode == 0

outer = "physical"
inner = "color"
payload = "orange"
source = f'{outer}.{inner} = "{payload}"\n'
result = subprocess.run(["./toml-decoder"], input=source, capture_output=True, text=True)
print(result.stderr, file=sys.stderr)
assert result.returncode == 0
decoded = json.loads(result.stdout)
assert decoded == {outer: {inner: {"type": "string", "value": payload}}}
=== END AC keys-dotted-round-trip ===

=== AC keys-redefinition-rejected ===
Intent: Defining the same key twice in one table is rejected with a non-zero exit.
Requires: executable=go; scope=test

import subprocess
import sys

build = subprocess.run(
    ["go", "build", "-o", "toml-decoder", "./cmd/toml-decoder"],
    capture_output=True, text=True,
)
print(build.stderr, file=sys.stderr)
assert build.returncode == 0

key = "name"
source = f'{key} = "Tom"\n{key} = "Pradyun"\n'
result = subprocess.run(["./toml-decoder"], input=source, capture_output=True, text=True)
print(result.stderr, file=sys.stderr)
assert result.returncode != 0
assert result.stdout == ""
=== END AC keys-redefinition-rejected ===

=== AC keys-suite-slice ===
Intent: The toml-test key slices execute and every key case passes.
Suite: scoped
Requires: executable=sh; scope=test
Requires: executable=go; scope=test
Requires: executable=toml-test; scope=test

import subprocess
import sys

pattern = "valid/key/**|invalid/key/**"
result = subprocess.run(
    ["sh", "sources/stage_test.sh", pattern],
    capture_output=True, text=True,
)
print(result.stdout)
print(result.stderr, file=sys.stderr)
assert result.returncode == 0
=== END AC keys-suite-slice ===

## User Acceptance

- None.

## Guardrails

- A key defined twice is an error, whether bare or quoted.
- Whitespace around dot-separated key parts is ignored.

# FEATURE: Parser Tables

| Field       | Value |
|-------------|-------|
| Version     | 20261014 V1 |
| Description | Standard table headers, implicit super-tables, arrays of tables, and their redefinition and ordering rules. |
| Depends On  | ARCHITECTURE.md, FEATURE-Parser-Keys.md |
| Provides    | table headers and arrays of tables in internal/toml |
| Consumes    | None |

## Questions

- None.

## Purpose

Parse `[table]` headers and `[[array]]` headers. Create implicit super-tables for `[a.b.c]`. Each `[[name]]` header appends a new table element to the array named `name`, and later sub-tables attach to the most recent element. Reject a standard table defined twice, and reject a `[[name]]` header that conflicts with a static table or static array.

## Programmatic Acceptance

=== AC tables-header-round-trip ===
Intent: A standard table header creates a nested table holding its keys.
Requires: executable=go; scope=test

import json
import subprocess
import sys

build = subprocess.run(
    ["go", "build", "-o", "toml-decoder", "./cmd/toml-decoder"],
    capture_output=True, text=True,
)
print(build.stderr, file=sys.stderr)
assert build.returncode == 0

table = "owner"
key = "name"
payload = "Regina"
source = f'[{table}]\n{key} = "{payload}"\n'
result = subprocess.run(["./toml-decoder"], input=source, capture_output=True, text=True)
print(result.stderr, file=sys.stderr)
assert result.returncode == 0
decoded = json.loads(result.stdout)
assert decoded == {table: {key: {"type": "string", "value": payload}}}
=== END AC tables-header-round-trip ===

=== AC tables-array-of-tables ===
Intent: Two array-of-tables headers produce a JSON array of two objects.
Requires: executable=go; scope=test

import json
import subprocess
import sys

build = subprocess.run(
    ["go", "build", "-o", "toml-decoder", "./cmd/toml-decoder"],
    capture_output=True, text=True,
)
print(build.stderr, file=sys.stderr)
assert build.returncode == 0

name = "products"
key = "sku"
first = "738594937"
second = "284758393"
source = f"[[{name}]]\n{key} = {first}\n\n[[{name}]]\n{key} = {second}\n"
result = subprocess.run(["./toml-decoder"], input=source, capture_output=True, text=True)
print(result.stderr, file=sys.stderr)
assert result.returncode == 0
decoded = json.loads(result.stdout)
assert decoded == {name: [
    {key: {"type": "integer", "value": first}},
    {key: {"type": "integer", "value": second}},
]}
=== END AC tables-array-of-tables ===

=== AC tables-duplicate-header-rejected ===
Intent: Defining the same standard table twice is rejected with a non-zero exit.
Requires: executable=go; scope=test

import subprocess
import sys

build = subprocess.run(
    ["go", "build", "-o", "toml-decoder", "./cmd/toml-decoder"],
    capture_output=True, text=True,
)
print(build.stderr, file=sys.stderr)
assert build.returncode == 0

table = "fruit"
source = f"[{table}]\napple = 1\n\n[{table}]\norange = 2\n"
result = subprocess.run(["./toml-decoder"], input=source, capture_output=True, text=True)
print(result.stderr, file=sys.stderr)
assert result.returncode != 0
assert result.stdout == ""
=== END AC tables-duplicate-header-rejected ===

=== AC tables-suite-slice ===
Intent: The toml-test table slices execute and every table case passes.
Suite: scoped
Requires: executable=sh; scope=test
Requires: executable=go; scope=test
Requires: executable=toml-test; scope=test

import subprocess
import sys

pattern = "valid/table/**|invalid/table/**"
result = subprocess.run(
    ["sh", "sources/stage_test.sh", pattern],
    capture_output=True, text=True,
)
print(result.stdout)
print(result.stderr, file=sys.stderr)
assert result.returncode == 0
=== END AC tables-suite-slice ===

## User Acceptance

- None.

## Guardrails

- A static table or static array may not be redefined by a `[[name]]` header.
- Implicit super-tables created by a header may later be defined explicitly.

# FEATURE: Parser Arrays Inline

| Field       | Value |
|-------------|-------|
| Version     | 20261014 V1 |
| Description | Arrays, inline tables, and the closure rule that forbids extending an inline table. |
| Depends On  | ARCHITECTURE.md, FEATURE-Parser-Strings.md, FEATURE-Parser-Lexical-Scalars.md, FEATURE-Parser-Keys.md |
| Provides    | array and inline-table parsing in internal/toml |
| Consumes    | None |

## Questions

- None.

## Purpose

Parse arrays of mixed value types, with nesting, optional trailing comma, and multi-line layout with comments. Parse inline tables on a single line with no trailing comma. An inline table is closed: keys cannot be added to it through dotted keys or table headers.

assert build.returncode == 0

key = "xs"
first = "1"
second = "2"
source = f"{key} = [{first}, {second}]\n"
result = subprocess.run(["./toml-decoder"], input=source, capture_output=True, text=True)
print(result.stderr, file=sys.stderr)
assert result.returncode == 0
decoded = json.loads(result.stdout)
assert decoded == {key: [
    {"type": "integer", "value": first},
    {"type": "integer", "value": second},
]}
=== END AC arrays-round-trip ===

=== END AC inline-table-round-trip ===

print(result.stderr, file=sys.stderr)

Intent: The toml-test array and inline-table slices execute and every case passes.
Suite: scoped
Requires: executable=sh; scope=test
Requires: executable=go; scope=test
Requires: executable=toml-test; scope=test

import sys

## User Acceptance

- None.

## Guardrails

- An inline table written with a trailing comma is rejected.
- Inline tables may not span lines unless a value inside them does.

# FEATURE: Parser Datetimes

| Field       | Value |
|-------------|-------|
| Version     | 20261014 V1 |
| Description | Offset date-time, local date-time, local date, and local time forms, with the fractional-second truncation rule. |

| Provides    | offset datetime, local datetime, local date, and local time decoding |
| Consumes    | None |

## Questions

- None.

# FEATURE: Conformance

| Field       | Value |
|-------------|-------|
| Version     | 20261014 V1 |
| Description | The terminal assembly story: the complete unfiltered toml-test suite run through the supplied scoring entry point. |
| Depends On  | ARCHITECTURE.md, FEATURE-Decoder-Contract.md, FEATURE-Parser-Strings.md, FEATURE-Parser-Lexical-Scalars.md, FEATURE-Parser-Lexical-Boundaries.md, FEATURE-Parser-Keys.md, FEATURE-Parser-Tables.md, FEATURE-Parser-Arrays-Inline.md, FEATURE-Parser-Datetimes.md |
| Provides    | sh sources/full_test.sh verdict |
| Consumes    | toml-decoder stdin/stdout contract |

## Questions

- None.

## Purpose

This is the only story that runs the complete suite. It runs `sh sources/full_test.sh` from the application root with no filter and takes its exit status as the verdict. The exit status is the whole verdict: the summary text and case counts are not asserted.

## Programmatic Acceptance

=== AC conformance-full-suite ===
Intent: The complete unfiltered conformance suite exits zero.
Suite: full
Requires: executable=sh; scope=test
Requires: executable=go; scope=test
Requires: executable=toml-test; scope=test

import subprocess
import sys

result = subprocess.run(
    ["sh", "sources/full_test.sh"],
    capture_output=True, text=True,
)
print(result.stdout)
print(result.stderr, file=sys.stderr)
assert result.returncode == 0
=== END AC conformance-full-suite ===

=== AC conformance-no-third-party ===
Intent: go.mod declares no required module, so no third-party TOML module is present.
Requires: executable=go; scope=test

from pathlib import Path

text = Path("go.mod").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
assert "require" not in text
=== END AC conformance-no-third-party ===

## User Acceptance

- None.

## Guardrails

- The scoring assets under `sources/` are read-only and are never modified or filtered.
- The conformance verdict is the exit status of `sh sources/full_test.sh` and nothing else.
